target). This revision resolves all 9:

- C1/C2 (core contradiction + fictional CLI): added an explicit scope
  note after the headline stating plainly what ships today
  (beadle-email) versus what's vision (the signed pipeline daemon --
  the mechanism the headline is named for). Reconciled the two most
  load-bearing FAQs (GPG knowledge, tech-risks mitigations) to
  distinguish what's actually built (ethos-based identity, isolated
  GNUPGHOME signing, whitelist binary resolution, --bare adversarial
  isolation) from what's still design (beadle init/sign/verify,
  Bridge health monitoring, service-manager integration, signature
  enforcement itself).
- C3/C4 (stale/contradictory validation FAQs): rewrote
  faq:customer-evidence and faq:next-step as one coherent, current
  narrative -- both Pipeline v1 and v2 shipped as tested code since
  v3.0, beadle-email alone has shipped five releases since, and the
  external validation test proposed at v3.0 still hasn't run because
  it structurally can't: no distribution, no onboarding, no signing
  enforcement.
- C5 (mischaracterized CVEs): re-researched via prfaq:researcher.
  CVE-2026-25253 was a gatewayUrl/WebSocket token-theft RCE, not a
  reverse-proxy auth bypass. CVE-2026-24763 was Docker PATH command
  injection, unrelated to the separate ClawHub malicious-skills
  supply-chain finding the doc had fused it with. Narrowed the closing
  claim: only the Snyk spoofed-email finding is the failure mode
  Beadle's trust model actually addresses.
- C6/C7/C8 (Feature Appendix): added a Must Do category (signing
  enforcement, beadle init, daemon distribution -- the actual
  launch-blockers). Rescoped "Shipped" to what a user can actually
  install (beadle-email only, tool count corrected 17->23). Moved
  Pipeline v1/v2 into a new "Built, Not Distributed" category. Renamed
  the Won't Do "Multi-identity support" to "Multi-tenancy" -- it
  flatly contradicted the Shipped "Multi-identity via ethos" entry
  under the same name.
- C9 (kill switch): pulled real numbers via gh api -- 3 GitHub stars
  against first release 2026-03-13, putting the 6-month kill-switch
  date at 2026-09-13, about two weeks out. Documented that "weekly
  binary downloads" can only mean beadle-email downloads today, since
  the daemon isn't distributed -- the metric doesn't measure the
  product the document is about.

Also addressed: stale version/citations (v0.14.1->v0.16.5, AutoGPT
182k->187k stars, added LangChain's 2025 follow-up survey, corrected

and a .md/.yaml command-file inconsistency.

Version bumped to v3.1. Six new citations added to prfaq.bib with
full source verification (SOCRadar, The Hacker News, GitHub Security
Advisory, Koi Security research, LangChain's 2025 survey, CNBC).
EOF
)"
